newsitem.title: UK: Britain's Blair denies Labour to cut union links.
newsitem.headline: Britain's Blair denies Labour to cut union links.

text.p: Britain's opposition Labour Party leader Tony Blair has denied reports that he is planning to cut the party's century-old ties with the trade unions, its principal paymasters.
His spokesman reacted after a string of newspaper reports said Blair was drawing up plans to sever the links if the unions provoke a wave of strikes during the first summer of a Labour government.

Four newspapers reported that Blair, opinion poll favourite to win the next general election due by May 1997, would ballot all party members on whether they wanted to cut ties to the unions, who founded the party.
Unions would then lose their voting rights at Labour Party conferences and on Labour's ruling bodies.
But a spokesman for Blair, a centrist eager to court middle- class voters, moved swiftly to deny any such plan.
"These stories have no foundation at all. Mr Blair made no such proposal and no such proposal is even under discussion," the spokesman said.

Labour's employment spokesman Stephen Byers said: "I understand four political correspondents are running a story based on a conversation I had with them. I said nothing to justify the ludicrous stories they are running tonight."
This week's Trade Unions Congress conference has been overshadowed by a row over Labour proposals to limit strikes by a system of binding arbitration.
Some unions believe Blair picked a fight to underline the new, more distant relationship between Labour and unions.
"The Labour Party will govern in government for the whole country," Blair said on Wednesday.
The unions provide half of Labour's funds and command half the votes at its policy-setting conference, but Blair sees the link as an electoral liability and has cut their influence.
